question: A cement kiln's reported specific heat consumption improves after a shift-clock correction, but fuel meter totals and clinker production are unchanged. How should an agent reconcile timestamp boundaries, meter rollover and clinker-tonnage attribution before treating the apparent improvement as real?
category: Kiln specific heat consumption time-boundary reconciliation
scenario: A revised shift start/end timestamp changes fuel-to-clinker allocation without an observed physical process change
evidence_required: Original and corrected timestamped fuel totalizer readings, meter units, rollover and calibration records
Clinker production scale records, silo transfers, kiln stops, residence-time lag and reporting boundary definitions
Fuel lower heating value basis, fuel mix, shift duration, energy conversion units and version-controlled calculation formulas
answer_and_decision_guide: Reconstruct the original and revised shift intervals from immutable meter readings; convert each fuel stream to a consistent energy basis and reconcile total energy and clinker tonnes over a longer unchanged reporting window. Account for kiln-to-cooler production lag and intermediate inventory rather than assuming instantaneous matching. If only shift allocation changes while the same cumulative fuel and clinker quantities remain, classify the difference as a reporting-boundary artifact, not an efficiency gain. Escalate unresolved calibration or production-balance differences to plant metrology and process engineers.
source_provenance: Seller-maintained blank comparison CSV is a free worksheet, not validated plant readings or an OEM method; verify its fields and formulas against site metering procedures.
free_first_decision: Use the free shift-comparison CSV and existing fuel, scale and shift logs before buying any reference material.

conditional_paid_check.authorization: Consider only an exact relevant inventoried file after verifying edition, rights, current price and explicit buyer approval; no automatic purchase.

model_limitations: Without raw time series, meter calibrations, inventory lag and LHV evidence, an AI cannot calculate a reliable SHC change or certify savings.
